reason: The idea survives the schedule and feasibility lens easily. Its implementation cost is overstated, and a dedicated slot is not the right way to ship it. (1) Mechanism checked in the source. experiments/ext_x138/biohub-x138.ipynb cell 0 l.70-74 sets KERNEL_START_TS and REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=27000. Cell 5 l.29-45 has _deadline_degrade(), which switches off relink (readmit is nested inside it), gap close, gap2, safe divisions and linefit. Cell 5 l.2114-2116 checks the deadline once per dataset while walking the geffs in sorted order. Cell 5 reads the value from env, so a cell-0 override is enough. (2) FACTUAL ERROR, in the idea's favour: there is no need to add a '--set' passthrough. tools/build_probe_kernel.py already accepts --set with --base x138 (l.1393-1399 parse, l.1522-1528 append to cell 0). I verified this on a scratchpad copy: `python tools/build_probe_kernel.py exp58_x138_deadline36k --base x138 --set REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=36000` builds cleanly. Only cell 0 differs from exp56, by one appended env line. Datasets, docker pin and machine shape are identical. The container work is ~10 min, not 1.5 h. It stacks with --patch divinsert for an exp57b variant. (3) Critical path, with the 26 Sep 00:00 UTC quota reset as the only hard wait: the first dummy commit can run 26 Sep 00:05-00:50, and the score lands 26 Sep ~08:30-11:00 UTC. That leaves ~70 h of slack to the 29 Sep 10:00 UTC cutoff, enough for 2-3 retries. P(scored in time) ~0.9. The residual risk is the user's OK / slot priority, a Kaggle hiccup, and a ~2-4% chance of a 12 h timeout, since a 10 h guard leaves ~2 h for the last full repair plus cells 6-11. (4) Caveats from this lens. (a) A free gate exists, the same one the value skeptic found. Submit-to-score latency is at least the kernel runtime, so if latency(#34) and latency(#35) < 7.5 h, the guard provably did not fire on those runs. Public and private come from ONE hidden run per submission, so those files' private scores are already fixed and the patch is worth exactly 0 for them. (b) The scored probe can barely validate anything. Public is expected to tie (LB noise 0.003), the private part is invisible, and the hidden-run logs are not visible. So a DEDICATED slot buys little information, and the change is only worth anything if it sits inside the file that becomes a final. (c) The optional second step needs new --patch code: keep safe divisions and linefit when degraded, plus the projected-finish print. That is ~1 h of agent work plus a second, forced-degrade dummy run (deadline 1 s -> 'DEADLINE:' on the first dataset and a valid CSV). That is also feasible on 26 Sep, but it is a code change and needs its own no-op sha256 test.
fix_if_any: Ship it as a zero-slot rider, not as its own probe. (1) Tonight, when #34/#35 score (25 Sep 17-20 UTC), the user reads their submit->score times on the submissions page. If latency < 7.5 h the guard did not fire in those runs and nothing more is needed for them. If latency >= 7.5 h, the patch becomes mandatory for the F1 candidate. (2) Either way, add `--set REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=36000` (no higher; keep >= 2 h of margin to 12 h) to EVERY x138-family candidate built from now on. That covers exp57b-type insertion, extra GPU passes, and any heavier tail, all of which reach the 27,000 s line earlier. The chosen F1 must be a submission that actually contains the patch. (3) Pre-registered dummy check: submission.csv sha256 equal to the unpatched twin (exp56 or exp57b) and no 'DEADLINE:' line. (4) Build the degradation-order patch only if latency >= 7.5 h. It keeps safe divisions and linefit and drops relink/readmit/gap2 first, with a budget test elapsed + remaining x max(60 s, 1.3 x p90 repair_s) > 39,600 s and a hard stop at 41,400 s. Validate it with a forced-degrade dummy run. (5) A dedicated slot is justified only if latency(#34 or #35) >= 8 h and no other x138-family probe is scheduled for 26 Sep.
realistic_public_gain: ~0 (<= +0.0005 expected). The x138 reproductions score a stable 0.953, which exceeds the unguarded exp51 at 0.950, so a public-side degradation is unlikely. Any residual is below LB noise (0.003).
realistic_private_gain: Expected ~+0.001-0.002 (guess: P(fire) 0.2-0.35 x P(degraded block private) ~0.7-0.8 x ~+0.006-0.02 conditional). Exactly 0 for any scored file whose latency < 7.5 h, and 0 or more once a patched run has scored validly.
critical_path: 25 Sep 17:00-20:00 UTC: #34/#35 score (dependency: base choice). The user or the laptop agent reads the submit->score latencies (free gate; browser/Kaggle API). 25 Sep ~20:00-20:30 UTC: on the user's laptop, the agent (the one with the repo and kaggle.json) runs `tools/build_probe_kernel.py exp58_x138_deadline36k --base x138 [--patch divinsert + exp57b's DIVINS_* knobs if #35 > #34] --set REPAIR_DEADLINE_S=36000`, ~10 min, already verified to build here. At the same time the user pre-approves the 26 Sep 00:xx submission before sleeping, as on 24 Sep 21:05. 26 Sep 00:05-00:50 UTC: after the GPU reset, the commit run of the kernel on the 4 dummy videos on vitaliineibauer (T4, ~0.7 of 30 GPU-h); check sha256 == unpatched twin and no DEADLINE line. 26 Sep ~01:00 UTC: submit, as a rider on the day's x138-family F1 candidate or as 1 of 5 slots. 26 Sep ~08:30-11:00 UTC: scored (7.5-10 h latency). Slack to 29 Sep 10:00 UTC: ~70 h (2-3 retry windows). Friend A is NOT on the critical path: kernel logs and latencies can come from the user's own Kaggle page or API. The optional degradation-order patch: agent ~1 h on 26 Sep morning + forced-degrade and no-op dummy runs (~1.4 GPU-h) + a 27 Sep slot, only if latency >= 7.5 h.
